# Take Note

Turn an informal update into a useful, correctly placed Markdown note. The user can speak or type a rough thought. The agent owns the routing work, while the user stays in control of the final knowledge base.

## When to Use

- User has an idea or thought they want to record
- User reports a blocker, status change, or event
- User mentions something they learned or want to remember
- User says "log this", "note this", "capture this", "take note that"

## Procedure

### 1. Understand the capture

Identify the core fact, relevant date, people or projects, and hints about its category. Infer reasonable detail from context. Ask one concise question only if it is necessary to route the note safely.

### 2. Route through maps

1. Begin at the root map.
2. Follow map links to the first specific folder or note that fits.
3. Prefer an active project or ongoing area over broad reference storage.
4. Use the inbox only when no stable home is clear.
5. Do not use a static path list as the routing mechanism.

If no suitable note exists, create a small kebab-case note in the best mapped folder and add it to that folder's map.

### 3. Preserve local context

Read the destination note before changing it. Match its headings, date format, list style, ordering, and terminology. Append or insert only the factual update in the appropriate section. Do not reorganize existing content as part of capture.

### 4. Maintain the graph

When a note or content directory is created, moved, renamed, or deleted, update the relevant parent map. Keep entries sorted and use vault-relative links.

### 5. Confirm

State the file or files updated and briefly summarize what was captured. Mention any new file and why it was created.

## Example

> “We finally agreed on the reporting-data owner in the design session.”

Route to the relevant project status note if one exists. Also record it in an accomplishments note only when it is clearly a meaningful career highlight. Read both targets first and preserve their existing format.
